claim: Lake Volta is the largest man-made lake in the world by surface area, about 8,500 km2.
qualification: Published figure 8,502 km2, shown rounded. Qualified "by surface area" throughout.

claim: At full capacity Lake Volta holds about 148 km3 (148 trillion litres).
qualification: Full-capacity figure; actual storage varies with water level.

claim: Lake Kariba covers about 5,600 km2, a smaller area than Lake Volta.
qualification: Published figure 5,580 km2, shown rounded.

claim: At full capacity Lake Kariba holds about 181 km3 (181 trillion litres) — more than thirty cubic kilometres more than Lake Volta.
qualification: 181 - 148 = 33 km3; full-capacity figures.

claim: Lake Volta's water would fill almost 30 billion 5,000-litre tanks.
qualification: Arithmetic: 148e12 L / 5,000 L = 29.6e9. Generic tank drawing, no brand implied.

claim: Lake Kariba is on average about one and a half times as deep as Lake Volta.
qualification: Published mean depths 18.8 m vs 29.2 m. Depth gauges labelled as published means, not surveyed profiles; containers labelled illustration.

claim: Out of every hundred working Ghanaians, about thirty-seven work in agriculture.

claim: That's around five million people.
qualification: About 5.0 million employed in agriculture, Q3 2025 (GSS QLFS).

claim: Out of every hundred cedis of economic output produced in 2025, about twenty-three came from agriculture.
verification_status: Reported by GSS (via GNA); release not yet checked directly
qualification: 22.8% of GDP, 2025 provisional. Real vs nominal share still to confirm in the GSS release.

claim: At the end of 2025, out of every hundred cedis Ghana's banks had outstanding in loans, just over four cedis were in agriculture.
verification_status: Chart reading; BoG data table not yet checked
qualification: 4.3% of total bank credit outstanding, Dec 2025 (BoG MPR Jan 2026, Fig 6.1). Total credit, not private-sector credit (4.5%), not new-lending flows.

claim: In 2025, agriculture grew by 6.8 percent, faster than the economy's overall growth of 6 percent.
verification_status: Reported by GSS (via GNA); release not yet checked directly
qualification: Real growth, 2025 provisional.

claim: Bank loans to agriculture actually went up.
qualification: ≈ GH¢4.49bn (Dec 2024) → ≈ GH¢4.77bn (Dec 2025), ≈ +6%; share × gross loans. Direction holds across the shares' rounding bands (+4% to +9%).

claim: But bank loans overall went up faster.
qualification: Gross loans GH¢111.0bn at Dec 2025, +16.2% y/y.

claim: So agriculture's share fell, from 4.7 percent to 4.3 percent.
verification_status: Chart reading; BoG data table not yet checked
qualification: Dec 2024 → Dec 2025, share of total bank credit outstanding.

claim: Now, these are bank loans, not every source of financing agriculture relies on.
qualification: BoG figures cover deposit money banks only; rural/community banks, microfinance, input credit and outgrower schemes are outside the measure.
